question: Can a deterministic 3D convolutional network approximately invert nonlinear cosmological structure formation and recover the corresponding linear displacement field without posterior sampling?

key_findings.claim: A reversed field-level V-Net recovers in-distribution linear displacement statistics accurately through moderately nonlinear scales.
key_findings.evidence: The model maps the final nonlinear Lagrangian displacement field to the Zel'dovich linear displacement field. On unseen pairs generated by the same forward emulator and fiducial cosmology, transfer-function error and stochasticity remain around 1-2% through k approximately 0.8-0.9 h/Mpc; forward-emulating the prediction agrees with the nonlinear target more closely for k below about 0.5 h/Mpc.

key_findings.claim: The task is substantially easier than reconstructing initial conditions from an astronomical survey.
key_findings.evidence: Input is the complete three-component nonlinear displacement Psi_NL(q) indexed by each particle's original Lagrangian grid coordinate q. Real surveys observe biased, sparse, noisy galaxy positions in redshift space without dark-matter particle identities or their unknown initial grid labels. The paper models none of these observation operators, masks, selection effects, or nuisance parameters.

key_findings.claim: Most favorable evidence is an inverse of a learned emulator, not of N-body dynamics itself.
key_findings.evidence: All 100 training nonlinear fields and all in-distribution test pairs come from the Jamieson et al. neural forward emulator at one fixed cosmology because N-body runs are described as too expensive. The main forward-consistency check also passes the inverse output through that same emulator, so shared approximation biases can make the cycle look better than an independent N-body resimulation would.

key_findings.claim: The stated cosmology conditioning cannot be learned from the reported training set.
key_findings.evidence: The network is said to receive Omega_m, but every one of the 100 training fields has the identical five-parameter cosmology, including Omega_m=0.300. A constant feature supplies no training variation from which to learn conditional dependence. Quijote tests vary all five parameters, while only Omega_m is input, so the OOD results measure accidental robustness rather than learned cosmological conditioning.

anchors.section: 3. Methodology: inputs and fixed training cosmology

key_findings.claim: The OOD study is qualitative and too sparse to support generalization across cosmology.
key_findings.evidence: Although Quijote provides 2,000 simulations, the paper ranks them by an ad hoc sum of relative differences in only Omega_m and sigma_8, plots single examples at six percentiles, and provides detailed plots for only the 0th and 20th percentiles. It reports no population mean, uncertainty, worst-case envelope, calibrated domain boundary, or comparison after retraining across cosmologies.

key_findings.claim: A deterministic point estimate does not resolve the one-to-many inverse problem or justify replacing posterior inference.
key_findings.evidence: Virialized small-scale configurations erase or scramble information, so conditional output is blurred inside halos. Power spectra and marginal Gaussian histograms can match while phase-level alternatives and uncertainty are absent. The authors ultimately propose the prediction as an initializer for sampling and list uncertainty estimation as future work, which is weaker than the abstract's suggestion that complex backward modeling may be unnecessary.

method.core_idea: Reverse an existing field-level V-Net: predict the linearly extrapolated Zel'dovich displacement field from the final nonlinear particle displacement field with a single deterministic forward pass.
method.mechanism: Train a three-level 3D encoder-decoder on 100 pairs of 128^3 Lagrangian-grid displacement fields in 250 Mpc/h boxes. Nonlinear targets are generated by a pretrained forward emulator at a fixed fiducial cosmology. The receptive field spans 96^3 cells, preserving very-large-scale linear behavior while learning local nonlinear corrections; evaluation uses one-point distributions, power spectra, cross-correlation, and emulator cycle consistency.
assumptions: The full dark-matter nonlinear displacement field and original particle-to-grid correspondence are observed.
The forward emulator's errors do not create shortcuts or systematic inverse bias.
A deterministic conditional point estimate is sufficient for downstream science despite nonidentifiability in halos.
Training on 100 fields at one cosmology covers enough field variation for other cosmologies and full N-body dynamics.
Power-spectrum transfer and stochasticity adequately measure scientific fidelity.
Periodic fixed-resolution simulation boxes transfer to different volumes and eventually to survey geometries.

techniques.role: Maps a 3D nonlinear displacement tensor to a 3D linear displacement tensor.
Produces paired nonlinear training targets without running new N-body simulations.
Learns medium-scale nonlinear corrections while leaving larger-scale linear relations implicit.
Measures amplitude agreement and phase stochasticity as functions of wavenumber.
Reapplies the learned forward model to predicted initial fields and compares resulting nonlinear statistics.

evaluations.setting: Held-out 128^3 fields generated by the same forward emulator at the one fiducial cosmology
evaluations.metric: One-point displacement histogram, transfer-function fractional error, and 1-r^2 stochasticity
evaluations.result: Marginals are close to the expected Gaussian except rare tails; spectral errors are about 1-2% up to k approximately 0.8-0.9 h/Mpc.
evaluations.baseline: Ground-truth linear fields; no reconstruction-method baseline

evaluations.setting: Predicted linear fields passed through the Jamieson et al. forward emulator
evaluations.result: Regenerated nonlinear fields agree well at large and medium scales, approximately k below 0.5 h/Mpc.

evaluations.setting: Selected Quijote N-body simulations with 512^3 particles, 1000 Mpc/h boxes, and varying five-parameter cosmologies
evaluations.metric: One-point and spectral plots at selected OOD percentiles
evaluations.result: The 0th and 20th percentile examples remain strong; plots visibly degrade toward higher heuristic dissimilarity percentiles.
evaluations.baseline: Ground-truth Quijote fields; no aggregate competitor or calibrated OOD baseline

limitations: The input assumes unobservable particle-level Lagrangian correspondences and is not a galaxy-survey observation model.
Training uses only 100 emulator-generated fields at one fixed cosmology, not full N-body pairs across parameter space.
Only Omega_m is nominally supplied, yet it is constant in training; the other varying cosmological parameters are omitted.
The deterministic output provides no posterior samples, epistemic uncertainty, aleatoric uncertainty, or calibrated abstention.
No direct comparison to standard reconstruction, the pre-existing CNN reconstruction paper, BORG, diffusion posterior sampling, or an identity/linear baseline is reported.
Cycle consistency is evaluated with the same learned forward emulator used to make training data.
OOD evidence consists mainly of individual percentile examples rather than statistics over the 2,000 Quijote simulations.
The title calls a z=0 linearly extrapolated displacement field 'initial conditions,' which is related to but not identical to a survey-ready primordial-state reconstruction.
No code, runtime table, seed variance, architecture ablation, training curve, noise study, resolution transfer, or downstream cosmological constraint is given.
failure_modes: The inverse network exploits artifacts of the forward emulator that are absent in an N-body simulator or real universe.
Multiple initial microstates map to one virialized halo and the deterministic network averages them into a field with correct power but incorrect phases.
A changed cosmology, gravity law, mass resolution, redshift, baryonic model, or neutrino sector shifts the inverse outside its training support.
Unknown particle labels, galaxy bias, redshift-space distortion, masks, and shot noise make the required displacement tensor unavailable.
Rare high-displacement regions are smoothed because they are underrepresented and strongly nonlinear.
Forward-cycle success masks error because inverse and forward networks share training distribution and inductive biases.
Power spectra match while halo identities, higher-order statistics, topology, and posterior coverage are wrong.
reusable_insights: A fast deterministic inverse can be valuable as a proposal or warm start even when a full posterior is ultimately required.
Separate simulation-state inversion from observation-to-state inference; the observation operator is often the harder scientific layer.
Never claim parameter conditioning when conditioning variables do not vary in training.
Validate learned inverse models by rerunning an independent high-fidelity simulator, not only the emulator that generated training pairs.
Report phase-sensitive, higher-order, object-level, downstream, and posterior-calibration metrics alongside power spectra.
open_questions: Does the inverse remain accurate when trained and tested exclusively on independent full N-body suites across cosmology and resolution?
Can the point estimate initialize BORG or diffusion sampling and measurably reduce effective sample cost without biasing the posterior?
How much information survives when the input is a masked, noisy, biased redshift-space galaxy field rather than labeled dark-matter displacements?
Can ensembles or conditional generative residuals represent only the nonidentifiable small-scale modes while retaining deterministic speed on large scales?
Which metrics predict downstream cosmological-parameter bias better than transfer-function error?
Can equivariance and multi-scale global context improve OOD transfer without learning box- or emulator-specific artifacts?

competitive_landscape.title: Reconstructing Cosmological Initial Conditions from Late-Time Structure with Convolutional Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Shallue and Eisenstein predates the target and already reconstructs initial linear density with a CNN, using standard reconstruction to undo nonlocal bulk flows and explicitly treating redshift-space distortions. The target predicts particle displacement directly with a V-Net and reports finer spectral agreement in its easier labeled-state setting, so its claim to pioneer deterministic CNN inversion is not supportable without narrowing the task distinction.

competitive_landscape.title: Posterior Sampling of the Initial Conditions of the Universe from Non-linear Large Scale Structures using Score-Based Generative Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Legin et al. infer full initial density fields from high-resolution N-body final density and sample a multimodal posterior marginalized over cosmological parameters. The target is much cheaper and produces one displacement estimate, but it cannot express lost small-scale information or uncertainty and is trained mainly against a forward emulator.

competitive_landscape.title: Bayesian Inference of Initial Conditions from Non-Linear Cosmic Structures using Field-Level Emulators
competitive_landscape.difference: Doeser et al. place a V-Net forward emulator inside BORG HMC, test noisy N-body mocks, return posterior initial conditions, and validate independent N-body resimulations through spectra, bispectra, halo mass functions, and profiles. It is computationally heavier but supplies the uncertainty and simulator-level validation absent from the target; the target could plausibly serve as its initializer.

competitive_landscape.title: Improving constraints on primordial non-Gaussianity using neural network based reconstruction
competitive_landscape.difference: Flöss and Meerburg train a U-Net on N-body density fields and evaluate whether reconstruction improves Fisher constraints, reporting roughly threefold gains for several primordial non-Gaussianity shapes. The target reports stronger field-level displacement spectra in its setup but offers no downstream parameter-inference test, making scientific utility harder to assess.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: A simple deterministic CNN can directly and cheaply recover trustworthy cosmological initial linear displacement fields from final nonlinear displacements, potentially avoiding expensive generative or Bayesian backward models.
novelty_assessment.evidence: A reversed V-Net trained on 100 emulator pairs reproduces one- and two-point statistics at the fiducial cosmology, maintains percent-level spectral metrics to moderately nonlinear wavenumbers, and shows qualitative robustness on selected Quijote N-body cosmologies.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The useful contribution is a compact demonstration that direct particle-displacement inversion can be an effective point estimator or proposal. It is not the first deterministic CNN reconstruction of cosmological initial conditions, and it does not solve the observational or posterior problem implied by the title. Fixed-cosmology emulator training, meaningless constant conditioning, same-emulator cycle validation, selected OOD examples, and the absence of uncertainty make claims that it can replace backward sampling premature.

reviewer_notes: Read all fourteen pages of the exact indexed workshop manuscript, including the complete formulation, training setup, all in-distribution and Quijote figures, spectral definitions, conclusion, appendices, and references. Source hashes and page count match fulltext_index.jsonl. Four direct official arXiv competitors were checked at current versions on 2026-08-23. The review particularly audits the missing citation to a pre-existing deterministic CNN reconstruction, the gap between labeled simulation displacements and survey observations, the constant Omega_m conditioning contradiction, and the circular same-emulator validation.
